solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Openly-expressed anger is present at birth

parts.note: something openly expressed is frank, said plainly
to anger someone is to incense them

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a fit of open rage is present when a baby is born.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the Nativity: frankincense was one of the gifts the Magi brought to the newborn Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankincense was one of the three gifts brought by the Magi to the infant Jesus, a present at a birth.

clue.text: Uncommitted voter's problem with viewer

definitions.meaning: a swing voter with no fixed party loyalty, who drifts between parties
the viewer is the eye; these are specks drifting across one's field of vision

explanation.surface: A fence-sitting voter turns out to have trouble with their television set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viewer' looks like a television viewer but means the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A swing voter drifts between parties; eye specks drift across sight; both senses come from drifting.

clue.text: Like broadcast on investigator of Central American language

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it
broadcast means the word is spoken aloud, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: like means as, in 'as good as gold'
tec is short for detective, an investigator

explanation.surface: A phrase seems to be about a broadcast concerning a researcher of a Central American tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investigator' is a detective, shortened in crossword slang; 'of' and 'language' only pad the surface around the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztecs were the people ruling much of Mexico before the Spanish conquest, so the word describes something from Central America.

clue.text: Information from knight at present on shelf

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king, also used for knight in crosswords
at present means now
a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: Information from a knight who is, at present, sitting on a shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge is facts and information that one has learnt; the two words are near synonyms.

clue.text: Straight and clear about answer

indicators.note: about means the word for clear is placed around the letter for answer

parts.note: to clear a sum is to net it, keeping it after deductions

explanation.surface: A response that is both direct and lucid about the answer to a question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Straight' is the drinks sense: a spirit served without water or a mixer.
explanation.definitionFit: A whisky served straight is undiluted, with no ice or mixer; neat means the same.

clue.text: A helping of crumpet here — always very light

indicators.note: A helping of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone praises a portion of crumpet served at this place as always airy and delicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal describes something extremely delicate and airy, as if not of this world.

clue.text: Go ahead, son — laugh!

parts.note: a hoot is a loud laugh

explanation.surface: A parent gives a son permission to go ahead and laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: As an exclamation, Shoot! invites someone to start speaking, the same as saying go ahead.

clue.text: Married one's boss in act of devilry

parts.note: one is I, and one's is read as I'S, giving IS
a chief is a boss

explanation.surface: A married woman's employer is up to some devilish behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief is playful or harmful naughtiness, which is what devilry describes.

clue.text: Domains concerned with charitable donations

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a business letter
alms are gifts of money given to the poor

explanation.surface: A heading about lands that deal with gifts to charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Realms are kingdoms or spheres of influence, the same as domains.

clue.text: Health professional with hot potatoes to be juggled ahead

indicators.note: ahead says the jumbled potatoes go in front of the letter for hot
juggled means the letters of potatoes are tossed into a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A juggler with hot potatoes is told about a medical practitioner.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of POTATOES gives OSTEOPAT, which is placed ahead of H; 'with' and 'to be' are linking words.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath treats bones and muscles by manipulation, so is a health professional.

clue.text: Ring, dainty, being held in reserve

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
nice can mean fine or delicate, as in a nice distinction

explanation.surface: A delicate ring is being kept back in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans put on ice are held back for later, kept in reserve for future use.

clue.text: Amuse the French on credit

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: on tick means on credit in British slang
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French shopkeeper is amused at buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: To tickle someone is to amuse or delight them, as in tickled pink.

clue.text: New port officer takes over procedure

indicators.note: takes means the pieces hold the next letter inside them
new means the letters of port are made anew in a different order

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A new harbour official takes control of the formalities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New port officer' reads as a harbour official, but 'New' only signals the rearrangement and 'officer' is a colonel.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocol is the accepted procedure or code of conduct for formal occasions.

clue.text: Travel around the borders of Eccles and live

indicators.note: around means the travel word goes about the picked letters

parts.note: to ride is to travel on a horse or vehicle

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An invitation to travel around the outskirts of Eccles and settle there.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccles is a town near Manchester. Its borders are E and S, placed inside RIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to have one's home there, which is to live there.

clue.text: Bearing up

definitions.meaning: upright, on one's feet rather than seated

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing up' reads as coping bravely, but the two words each define separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing can mean tolerating something, and also being on one's feet, upright.

clue.text: Storerooms for ladies' underwear worn by king!

indicators.note: worn by means the king letter is dressed in the underwear, put inside it

parts.note: panties are women's knickers
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Cupboards for storing ladies' knickers that have been worn by the king!
explanation.definitionFit: Pantries are small rooms used for storing food and kitchen goods.

clue.text: Flog antique sill

parts.note: to thresh is to beat, as with grain or a thrashing
antique means old

explanation.surface: An instruction to sell off an old windowsill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' reads as British slang for sell, but here it means beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A threshold is the sill of a doorway, the strip of wood or stone one steps over.

clue.text: Obvious cartel plotted to hoard copper

indicators.note: to hoard means to keep something hidden inside, so the metal goes within
plotted means the letters of cartel are schemed into a new arrangement

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: It is clear a scheming cartel planned to stockpile copper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plotted' reads as conspiring in the surface; here it signals the rearrangement of cartel's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clear-cut is plain and definite, with no doubt left, which is obvious.

clue.text: How people might argue about the delay?

indicators.note: about here means the letters of the delay are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about the way people would row over a hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: People who argue heatedly do so angrily and with passion, which is how a row goes.

clue.text: Youth culture's fast-food establishment with no starters

indicators.note: with no starters means each word loses its first letter

parts.note: a chip shop is a British takeaway selling fish and chips

explanation.surface: Young people's favourite takeaway serves no first courses.
explanation.walkthrough: CHIP SHOP loses the first letter of each word, C and S. A chip shop is a British fish-and-chips takeaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip-hop is the music and street culture of rap, breakdancing and graffiti associated with young people.

clue.text: Play for time before search

indicators.note: before puts the time letter ahead of the search word

parts.note: to rifle is to search through hastily

explanation.surface: Someone stalls for time before a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle with something is to toy with it, to play idly without care.

clue.text: I heard graduate students getting something in orbit

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken by its sound when said aloud

parts.note: the letter I spoken sounds like the word for the organ of sight
BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
L is a learner, a student driver; two of them give LL

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have heard graduate students launching something into space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orbit' looks astronomical but means the eye socket.
explanation.definitionFit: The orbit is the bony socket in the skull that holds the eyeball.

clue.text: Stand, if poorly seated, surrounded by political outsiders

indicators.note: surrounded by means the jumbled letters go inside the picked letters
the outsiders of a word are its first and last letters
poorly means the letters of seated are badly placed, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A seat badly placed among political outsiders still has to stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' looks like a verb but is the noun, a base for a statue.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base or stand on which a statue or column is mounted.

clue.text: Dull person's standing order covering total

indicators.note: covering means the order's letters wrap around the total word

parts.note: SO is the abbreviation for a standing order, a regular bank payment
to total is to add up

explanation.surface: A bore's bank payment instruction covers the full sum.
explanation.walkthrough: A saddo is British slang for a pathetic, boring person.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddo is British slang for a sad, socially inadequate and boring individual.

clue.text: A prop on dry land

parts.note: to shore up is to prop; a shore is a supporting beam

explanation.surface: A support placed on firm ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on the shore or on land, as opposed to at sea.

clue.text: Japanese city with large area occupied by a king

indicators.note: occupied by means the first pieces are filled by the later ones placed inside

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize, very large
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A Japanese city with a large territory taken over by a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major port and the third largest city of Japan.

clue.text: Sanctimonious article supporting southern city

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporting piece goes below the one it holds up

parts.note: pi is short for pious, sanctimonious
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A self-righteous essay backing a southern town.
explanation.walkthrough: PISA is the Italian city of the leaning tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisa is a city in Tuscany, Italy, famous for its leaning bell tower.

clue.text: Had nothing women need, excepting one tab

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing

indicators.note: excepting means one letter is left out of need

parts.note: E is ecstasy, the drug sold as tablets, so a tab

explanation.surface: Someone had nothing that women need, apart from a single tablet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need' has two Es; only one is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Owned is the past tense of own, to possess, which is what had means here.

clue.text: Dubiously tail chap pinching old banger

indicators.note: pinching means the jumbled letters grab and hold the next piece inside
dubiously means the letters of tail chap are set out in a doubtful new order

explanation.surface: A shady fellow with a tail nicks an old car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger' is British slang for a sausage, not an old car. TAIL CHAP rearranged gives CHIPLATA, holding O.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a small thin sausage, and banger is British slang for a sausage.

clue.text: Ferociously sound horn — pass unknown trouble

parts.note: to toot is to sound a horn
to hand is to pass something over
N is an unknown quantity in algebra
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A driver honks furiously and passes trouble of an unknown kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting tooth and nail means with all one's ferocity and might, using every means.
